study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Expand and share pre-trained normative models to include surface area and resting-state functional connectivity, and benchmark whether deviation scores from normative models outperform raw features for group differences (schizophrenia vs controls), classification, and prediction of general cognitive ability.

nm1_model_origin.detail: Structural: Pre-trained warped Bayesian Linear Regression models on ~58,000 typical participants across many sites (age, sex, Euler, site covariates). Functional: New pre-trained models on ~22,000 typical participants across many sites (age, sex, mean FD, site covariates); evaluated on held-out test and transferred to unseen sites (UMich, COBRE).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Normative-model deviation features outperform raw features for SZ vs HC group differences and classification (notably for cortical thickness); regression gains are modest and not statistically significant.
